risks.risk_name: Personal apps on company phone accessing corporate resources
risks.evidence: user has a company-provided Android phone; the company Android phone is used for work-related tasks
risks.description: Allowing personal use or installation of personal apps on corporate phones increases the chance that third‑party apps will access corporate information or introduce malware.
risks.possible_consequence: Data exfiltration, compromise of corporate accounts and contact lists, and increased risk of targeted attacks using harvested information.

risks.risk_name: Increased phishing and mail-based attack surface via mobile email

risks.risk_name: Document exfiltration from mobile access
risks.evidence: the Android phone is used to access work documents
risks.description: Work documents accessed on the phone can be copied, synced or uploaded by apps or users to external services or personal accounts.
risks.possible_consequence: Unauthorized disclosure of sensitive documents, leakage of intellectual property or regulated data, and compliance violations.

risks.risk_name: Third-party cloud and app dependency leading to data exposure
risks.evidence: the company Android phone is used for work-related tasks; the Android phone is used to access work documents
risks.description: Mobile access often involves third-party cloud services and apps; vulnerabilities or misconfigurations in those external services can expose corporate data.

risks.risk_name: Insufficient device management and operational controls for mobile
